Create a hexagon grid that tiles a geometry

Source: R/map-tile.R
hex_grid.Rd

Tiles a geometry with exactly n_tiles equally sized hexagons. The hexagon size is chosen so that n_tiles hexagons have the same total area as the geometry, and the hexagons that overlap the geometry the most are kept.

Usage

hex_grid(object, n_tiles = NROW(object), island_gap = 0.5, crs = NULL)

Arguments

object

An sf object, or a geometry column (sfc), to tile. It is recommended to first simplify the geometry to speed up the tiling.

n_tiles

The number of hexagons. Defaults to one for each region of object.

island_gap

The distance, in hexagon widths, beyond which landmasses are tiled as separate islands. Use Inf to tile all land together.

crs

The projected coordinate reference system to make the hexagons in, such as the one the map will be plotted in. object is transformed to crs with sf::st_transform(). Defaults to the CRS of object, or for longitude/latitude input, to a Lambert azimuthal equal-area CRS centred on the data ("+proj=laea +lat_0=... +lon_0=...").

Value

A geometry column (sfc) of n_tiles hexagons that tile the input geometry, in the coordinate reference system they were made in.

Details

Landmasses that are further apart than island_gap hexagon widths are tiled separately. The hexagons of different landmasses are always separated by at least one empty hexagon, so islands such as Tasmania remain visibly distinct from the mainland. When object has several regions, each landmass gets a share of the n_tiles hexagons in proportion to its number of regions (so by default, exactly one hexagon for each of its regions, as in hexmap()). A single geometry is shared between its landmasses in proportion to their area.

hex_grid() and hex_allocate() are the two steps of an ungrouped hexmap(): hexmap(x) is the same as hex_allocate(x, hex_grid(x)). Grouped hexagon maps are instead made by a layout.

Examples

library(sf)
election <- st_transform(aus_election_2025, 3577)
# A hexagon for each electoral division
grid <- hex_grid(election)
# The outline of Australia with 75 hexagons
australia <- st_union(election)
grid <- hex_grid(australia, n_tiles = 75)

library(ggplot2)
ggplot() +
  geom_sf(data = australia) +
  geom_sf(data = grid, fill = "steelblue", alpha = 0.2)
